In this VladTV interview, Carlos Lehder reflects on his early life in Armenia, Colombia, his German father’s move to South America, and the pull of New York City culture, money, and rock and roll. Lehder details how he drifted from restaurant work into a stolen rental car ring involving Hertz and Avis vehicles near Kennedy Airport, leading to his first prison sentence. He then discusses entering marijuana smuggling and transporting cocaine from Bolivia to Colombia before the drug trade expanded into the U.S. market.

A key moment comes when Lehder recalls serving time at the federal prison in Danbury, Connecticut, where he met George Jung, also known as “Boston George,” who was incarcerated for flying marijuana from Mexico to California. Lehder explains how their conversations shifted toward cocaine trafficking and shares the hard lessons he later learned from the Medellín Cartel era with Pablo Escobar.

William Noguera sits down with VladTV to discuss his early life in Los Angeles and La Puente, California, his Colombian-American upbringing, martial arts training, and the violent home environment that shaped him. Convicted of murder at 18, Noguera spent 42 years in San Quentin Prison, much of it on death row.  

In this interview, he recounts becoming a hapkido champion, stealing high-end cars, and operating in Southern California during an era when Mexican gangs and the Mexican Mafia were expanding influence. Noguera also details the turbulent relationship with his pregnant teenage girlfriend, allegations of abuse in her home, and the events leading to the killing of her mother, Navarro, after a confrontation involving a martial arts baton.  

Now 62, Noguera reflects on rage, steroids, accountability, the police investigation, and the life-changing consequences of one violent night in 1983.

Retired Marine Raider and Scout Sniper Cody Alford sits down with VladTV to reflect on his path from Texas teenager to combat Marine after 9/11, and the brutal realities he faced in Iraq. Alford details his role with 2nd Battalion, 1st Marines during the Battle of Fallujah, where 95 U.S. service members were killed and 560 wounded, including surviving a headshot to his Kevlar helmet on his first day in the city. He describes close-quarters firefights, Echo Company, Delta Force support, Operation Steel Curtain, Ramadi, foreign fighters, Saddam Hussein’s former compounds, and the toll of urban warfare. Alford also discusses deployments to Afghanistan, the Taliban, the U.S. withdrawal, PTSD, traumatic brain injuries, veterans’ mental health, and his post-military life. The conversation expands to war, media narratives, Israel-Palestine, Iran, and the human cost of combat.

Robinhood co-founder Vlad Tenev sits down with DJ Vlad to revisit the height of the GameStop trading frenzy, including the viral Clubhouse exchange where Elon Musk pressed him over whether Robinhood had acted improperly. Tenev explains why that public conversation became a turning point in changing perception after earlier interviews he now calls “corpo nonsense,” and describes being new in the CEO role during Covid as the crisis unfolded.

The discussion covers Robinhood restricting new positions, accusations from traders who believed GameStop could keep climbing, criticism from skeptics who said the meme stock chaos should never have happened, and the painful reality for investors who bought near the top and lost money. Tenev also addresses risk management, short selling, market structure, settlement periods for U.S. stocks, and how the fallout helped push Robinhood toward tokenization efforts.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Vincent Marino reflects on walking free in August 2024 after serving more than 28 years behind bars, entering prison in 1996 and returning to a world transformed by the internet, smartphones, and modern life. Marino describes missing the funerals of close family members, surviving prison through discipline, fitness, legal work, and a positive mindset, and witnessing the toll long sentences can take on inmates.

He also explains how time in the law library led him to help prisoners pursue compassionate release, appeals, sentencing guideline changes, and relief under new case law. Marino discusses Allenwood Medium, Coleman in Florida, the First Step Act of 2018, the Supreme Court’s Taylor decision, Chief Judge Mike Wolf, and cases involving inmates like Burgess and a Charlestown prisoner. He recalls receiving $41 upon release and seeing cash for the first time in decades.
